name: Build it, break it: the failure lab

why.matters: You recognise a failure quickly only if you've seen it before. Breaking a model on purpose, in a safe copy, builds that recognition without waiting for a production incident.
why.failure: A team spends two days on a "random" wrong total that anyone who had seen bi-directional ambiguity would have spotted in minutes.
why.use: For each failure: build the working version, break it deliberately, observe the symptom, diagnose it with tools, fix it, explain it in two sentences, and write the check that prevents it.
why.avoid: Doing this on a shared or production model. Always work on a copy.

verified.context: Power BI Desktop (Sept 2026): relationships, Performance Analyzer, View Native Query, incremental refresh

refs.title: Data reduction techniques for Import models

asg.brief: In a copy of the starter project, make the relationships misbehave in two ways and learn the symptoms.
req: Build: Net Sales by RegionName from DimRegion and by the customer's region, as in Beginner.
Break 1: set DimCustomer ↔ FactSales to bi-directional and add DimCustomer[RegionKey] → DimRegion. Observe what Power BI does and what your visuals show.
Break 2: make FactSales → DimRegion inactive. Observe the totals.
For each: the symptom, how you diagnosed it, the fix, a two-sentence explanation, and the check that would have caught it.
asg.exp: Break 1: Power BI refuses or deactivates a relationship because of an ambiguous path (or results depend on which path wins). Break 2: every region shows the grand total. Checks: no bi-directional relationships without an ADR; a test that regional totals sum to the grand total and differ from each other.

asg.ds: enterprise pack (1M rows) or starter project
asg.brief: Generate a larger fact (Resources → Enterprise scale pack) and make it slow on purpose, three ways, measuring each with Performance Analyzer and DAX Studio.
req: An iterator that evaluates a measure per row of the fact (e.g. SUMX(FactSales, [Net Sales]) or FILTER over the fact with a measure inside).
A calculated column on the fact with a high-cardinality result (e.g. a timestamp as text).
A query that stops folding (a custom function per row before a filter).
asg.exp: The iterator shows many storage-engine queries or callbacks and FE time; the calculated column inflates model size (VertiPaq Analyzer) and refresh; the broken folding shows a greyed-out View Native Query and a longer refresh. Each fix restores the baseline.

asg.brief: Simulate the two most common refresh failures and write the runbook entry for each.
req: Schema drift: rename a column in a source CSV that the model uses.
Incremental refresh misconfigured: RangeStart/RangeEnd filter on a column that doesn't fold, or with >= on both ends.
For each: the error or symptom, the diagnosis, the fix, the prevention.
asg.exp: Schema drift: "The column … wasn't found" naming the table; fix the step or the source; prevent with a data contract. Incremental: duplicated or missing rows at partition boundaries (>= on both ends) or a full scan every refresh (no folding); fix with >= RangeStart and < RangeEnd on a foldable column.

int.a: So that you recognise the symptom quickly when it happens for real. The second time you see an ambiguous relationship or a broken fold, you diagnose it in minutes instead of days.

int.q: What symptom suggests an ambiguous relationship path?
int.a: Power BI refusing to activate a relationship, a relationship silently made inactive, or totals that change depending on which filters are applied, especially after adding a bi-directional relationship.

int.q: Why does >= RangeStart AND <= RangeEnd break incremental refresh?
int.a: Rows exactly on the boundary match two adjacent partitions and are loaded twice. Use >= RangeStart AND < RangeEnd so each row belongs to exactly one partition.

int.q: What is schema drift and how do you defend against it?
int.a: A source changes structure (renamed, removed or retyped columns). Defend with data contracts and change notification, select columns by name explicitly, fail loudly with a clear error, and monitor refresh failures.

ass.q: Making FactSales → DimRegion inactive, with no other change, makes a matrix by RegionName show:
o: The grand total on every row
ass.why: Without an active path, the region filter doesn't reach the fact, so every row shows the total.

ass.q: View Native Query is greyed out on a Power Query step against SQL Server. This means:
o: Folding stopped at or before this step
ass.why: Steps after a non-foldable step run in the mashup engine.

ass.q: Write a one-page "failure field guide": for each failure from this lab, symptom → likely cause → first diagnostic step.
ass.hint: This is the start of your team's runbook (Templates → Runbook).
